evidence: Clear separation into logical modules (app/api, app/auth, app/main) with dedicated __init__.py files and cohesive responsibilities
Shared database via SQLAlchemy (models.py), indicating single data store
Flask app factory pattern (create_app in app/__init__.py) with config.py supporting multiple environments
Blueprints used for modular routing (api, auth, main), but all within one application process
No inter-service communication patterns (no REST clients, message queues, or gRPC clients between modules)
Tests co-located with source (tests/), using same app instance and models, indicating tight integration
Migrations managed centrally via Alembic, pointing to one database schema
Low package count (5) and shallow directory depth (3) consistent with a single deployable unit
risks: Potential for tight coupling between modules if dependencies are not carefully managed
Scaling requires horizontal duplication of entire monolith rather than individual services
Single point of failure for all functionality
Deployment changes may require full rebuild and restart despite modularity
